mercy_translation.text:
The Jews, then, are inventing stories and postponing the present time. For when did prophet or vision cease from Israel except now, when Christ, the Holy of Holies, has come? A great sign and mark of the presence of God the Word is precisely that Jerusalem no longer stands, no prophet is raised up, and no vision is revealed to them—and this is entirely fitting.

For once the One signified has come, what further need is there for those who signified him? Once the truth is present, what further need is there for the shadow? For this reason they prophesied until the self-righteousness came and the One who redeems the sins of all. For this reason Jerusalem stood for so long: so that there the types of the truth might be rehearsed beforehand.

Therefore, with the Holy of Holies present, vision and prophecy have fittingly been sealed and the kingship of Jerusalem has ceased. Kings were anointed among them only until the Holy of Holies was anointed. Moses too prophesies that the kingdom of the Jews would stand until his coming, saying: “A ruler shall not fail from Judah, nor a leader from his thighs, until the things laid up for him come; and he is the expectation of the nations.”

For this reason the Savior himself cried out: “The law and the prophets prophesied until John.” If there is now among the Jews a king, prophet, or vision, then they rightly deny the Christ who has come. But if there is neither king nor vision, if all prophecy has now been sealed and the city and temple have been taken, why do they act so impiously and transgress so far as to see what has happened yet deny Christ who brought these things about?

Why, seeing people from the nations abandoning idols and placing their hope in the God of Israel through Christ, do they deny the Christ who according to the flesh came from the root of Jesse and now reigns? If the nations were worshiping some other god and did not confess the God of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and Moses, they might reasonably make the excuse that God had not come.

But if the nations worship the God who gave the law to Moses, who made the promise to Abraham, and whose word the Jews dishonored, why do they not recognize—or rather, why do they deliberately overlook—that the Lord foretold by the Scriptures has shone upon the inhabited world and appeared to it bodily, as Scripture says: “The Lord God has appeared to us”; and again, “He sent his Word and healed them”; and again, “Not an elder, not an angel, but the Lord himself saved them”?

They suffer something like a person whose mind is deranged: he sees the earth illuminated by the sun yet denies the sun that illuminates it. What more is the One they expect supposed to do when he comes? Call the nations? They have already been called. Bring prophecy, king, and vision to an end? This too has already happened. Expose the godlessness of idols? It has already been exposed and condemned. Abolish death? It has already been abolished.

What, then, has not happened that Christ must still do? What remains unfulfilled so that they may now rejoice in disbelief? For if, as we see, they now have neither king, prophet, Jerusalem, sacrifice, nor vision, while the whole earth has been filled with the knowledge of God and people from the nations abandon godlessness and flee for refuge to the God of Abraham through the Word, our Lord Jesus Christ, then it should be clear even to those most shamelessly resistant that Christ has come, enlightened all people with his own light, and taught the true and divine teaching concerning his Father.

From these and many more passages in the divine Scriptures one may fittingly answer Jewish objections.

translator_notes: Translated directly from the Greek source.
This is a highly polemical late-antique Christian argument about prophecy, temple, and messianic fulfillment; Mercy should display historical-context guidance alongside it.
Translation preserves Athanasius' argument without endorsing contempt toward Jewish people.
